warnings.warning: T is multiplied directly by the square root of V_E and added to an offset without a fitted coefficient or unit conversion. The claimed half-order magnitude does not close the dimensions of a 122-day decomposition fraction, and the temperature multiplier is not derived from the cited trait relation.

The log base, zero-rate handling, coefficient evidence, residuals, and observed M-versus-log(V_D) points are absent. Exponentiating and reparameterizing the asserted relation is algebraically clear, but the current paper supplies no data display or uncertainty supporting the relation it later fits.

The extension component, exponential moisture component, and intercept are added without a dimensional argument, interaction term, model-form comparison, or range constraint. The paper does not show that this additive form is preferable to alternatives or remains inside V_D in [0,1].

The response is called an Arrhenius diagram, but its exponent uses V_Emax divided by T times H rather than activation energy divided by a gas constant and absolute temperature. Extension rate, temperature, and humidity do not form an evidently dimensionless exponent, so the physical Arrhenius interpretation is unsupported.

The official moisture trade-off is described as competitive ranking minus moisture niche width, yet Equation 6 replaces it with a linear transform of an ambient-humidity lower limit. No paired data, scale reconciliation, or biological calibration establishes that these two constructs are equivalent.

Equation 7 declares lambda, a, and K to be arbitrary real numbers, but a^M is not generally real for a negative a and noninteger M; Table 2 uses fractional negative M. The optimization needs at least a positivity constraint on a and a stated admissible domain.

The fitting dataset is referenced only as an appendix of [5]. The paper omits N, the actual {T,V_E,M,V_D} rows, exclusions, duplicate handling, units, and any train/validation split, so the objective and reported coefficients cannot be independently reconstructed.

The learning rate r, iteration budget I, sample count N, sampling order, seed, numerical precision, and stopping rule are not reported. A reader cannot reproduce the SGD path or determine whether the final iterate is stable to hyperparameters or initialization.

The a update does not enforce a>0 even though later evaluations use a^M with fractional negative M. Crossing zero can make the objective or gradient non-real, and the paper supplies no reparameterization, projection, feasibility check, or gradient verification.

One coefficient triple is transferred to every species and environment without species effects or uncertainty. The fitted response is not constrained to the declared V_D range [0,1], and the paper does not report how negative or above-one predictions are handled before conversion to decomposition time.

The fitted response is not constrained to the declared V_D range [0,1], and the paper does not report how negative or above-one predictions are handled before conversion to decomposition time.

For positive V_E, sigmoid(1/V_E) decreases from near 1 toward 0.5 as V_E increases. This directly contradicts the prose claim that P_E increases with extension rate and means the proposed probability transform reverses the intended rate ordering.

The set update adds a generic (p,q) after prose discusses an uninfected cell adjacent to F_i, but the equation does not encode neighborhood, eligibility, simultaneous claims, species collision priority, or update ordering. Removal timing relative to addition and grid-label updates is also incomplete.

The set update adds a generic (p,q) after prose discusses an uninfected cell adjacent to F_i, but the equation does not encode neighborhood, eligibility, simultaneous claims, species collision priority, or update ordering. Removal timing relative to addition and grid-label updates is also incomplete.

If N_i^{t+1}=|F_i^{t+1}| is computed after Equation 17 removes fully decomposed cells, subtracting N_Di^t again double-counts removals. The expression is also called dN_i/dt although it is a discrete difference with no division by or definition of the time step.

The correction factor c=5x10^6 is asserted without derivation or calibration. Dividing a global 122-day mass-loss fraction by 500^2 makes cell time depend on arbitrary grid resolution, while cell mass, rounding, zero/negative V_D handling, and resolution invariance are absent.

The prose resets fully decomposed cells to G(p,q)=1 to simulate falling leaves, but Equation 20 only removes coordinates from F_i and contains no renewal arrival process, timing, or resource amount. This hidden nutrient input affects both late stabilization and decomposition totals.

For a remaining factor between 0 and 1, dividing V_E by that factor makes 1/[V_E(1-occupancy)] larger, so the sigmoid P_C is larger than P_E, not lower as the prose claims. Together with Equation 15, the algebra reverses the intended competitive suppression.

The competitive CA inherits the zero-rate singularity, occupancy-denominator failure, reversed probability direction, hidden renewal, collision ambiguity, and uncalibrated decomposition time. Replacing one probability does not by itself establish a biologically valid interaction model.

main_argument_chains.claim: A literature-shaped nonlinear relation converts species and environmental traits into decomposition rate.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the transparent component-to-fit organization while requiring unit closure, row-level fitting data, constraints, holdout error, and uncertainty before transfer.

main_argument_chains.claim: Extension and decomposition outputs can parameterize a spatial cellular decomposition process.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Learn the named-interface architecture, but require monotonicity, time/grid scaling, initialization, neighborhood, collision, renewal, and stochastic-replication specifications.

main_argument_chains.claim: Replacing the baseline probability with an occupancy-modified probability produces a measurable competition effect.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Preserve the ablation-style comparison while treating global occupancy as a constructed competition proxy pending domain proof and biological calibration.

main_argument_chains.claim: Environmental and regional inputs change trajectory ordering and yield conditional species rankings.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain aligned within-species and within-region panels, but require climate distributions, time series, explicit ranking horizons, tie rules, uncertainty, and atmospheric-trend forcing for decisions.

main_argument_chains.claim: The all-three modeled community decomposes faster than each single-species case in repeated simulation.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Notation ledger. Purpose: stabilize the hybrid relation-to-CA vocabulary. Encodings: symbol, definition, range or unit, and definition cross-reference. Claim: the paper separates environmental inputs, rates, sets, probabilities, and times. Construction: compact two-column table.

Six-species parameter ledger. Purpose: expose the scenario traits. Encodings: rows by fungus; T_max, V_Emax, H_l, and M columns. Claim: species differ in optimum, extension ceiling, and moisture trait. Construction: literature values plus Equation 6-derived M.

Temperature-response curves. Purpose: show the two-branch optimum shape. Encodings: T on x, V_E on y, three V_Emax colors, dashed T_max. Claim: realized extension peaks at the optimum and declines afterward.

Humidity-response curves. Purpose: show monotone humidity response under fixed temperature. Encodings: H on x, V_E on y, three V_Emax colors. Claim: humidity increases realized extension within the proposed relation.

Unfitted composite rate-system block. Purpose: retain the entire dependency interface in one view. Encodings: decomposition equation, parameter domain, moisture transform, two environmental branches, outside-domain zero.
Nonlinear fitting objective. Purpose: show observations, prediction, unknowns, and squared residuals together. Encodings: argmin plus per-sample prediction.
SGD procedural table. Purpose: expose input, initialization, cyclic sample loop, three updates, and final iterate. Encodings: numbered pseudocode.
Dual-axis optimization trace. Purpose: inspect numerical behavior. Encodings: noisy blue loss, orange lambda, iteration x-axis. Claim: loss becomes smaller and lambda approaches 31.9.
Fitted calculation-system block. Purpose: freeze coefficients and preserve the environment-to-rate interface. Encodings: fitted decomposition plus moisture and piecewise extension equations.

Extension-to-cellular interface block. Purpose: convert rate to probability, set updates, removal, and count change. Encodings: sigmoid, piecewise stochastic update, set subtraction, reported derivative.
Decomposition-time interface. Purpose: map 122-day response to cell completion delay. Encodings: inverse rate, grid area, correction factor.
Baseline CA system. Purpose: assemble transition, random draw, extension probability, and decomposition time. Encodings: brace-delimited equations.
Baseline final spatial map. Purpose: show simultaneous three-species infection and decomposed cells. Encodings: 500-by-500 color grid and categorical legend.
Baseline population trajectories. Purpose: reveal early peaks, decline, and late separation. Encodings: three colored N_i lines over days.
Baseline population-change trajectories. Purpose: align phase interpretation with a change metric. Encodings: three colored dN_i/dt lines.
CA pseudocode. Purpose: make grid scanning and state updates inspectable. Encodings: nested time/cell loops, adjacency, probability, delay, update, and outputs.
Competition interface and composite CA. Purpose: isolate the one probability change between baseline and competition. Encodings: occupancy factor, reciprocal sigmoid, reused transition and delay.
Competitive final spatial map. Purpose: compare decomposed coverage with Figure 3. Encodings: same grid and species colors.
Competitive population trajectories. Purpose: support the 33.65 percent late-count comparison. Encodings: same species colors and day axis as baseline.
Competitive population-change trajectories. Purpose: compare early change and late near-zero behavior. Encodings: three dN_i/dt lines.
End-to-end dependency graph. Purpose: show input, equation, derived quantity, model, and feedback handoffs. Encodings: blue input boxes, teal equation labels, yellow model boxes, arrows.
Four-panel T-H sensitivity comparison. Purpose: test late species ordering under controlled environment changes. Encodings: aligned axes and species colors; panel titles give exact T and H.

Six-by-five individual-environment trajectory matrix. Purpose: compare each species across five named environments. Encodings: six species panels, five consistent environment colors, common 100-day horizon.
Five regional competitive-combination panels. Purpose: identify scenario-specific dominant and inferior species. Encodings: one region per panel, three labeled trajectories.
Regional input ledger. Purpose: reveal T, H, and coordinate assumptions behind Figures 7-8. Encodings: five region rows and four numeric columns.
Two-panel diversity comparison. Purpose: show multi-versus-single decomposition curves and 1000 per-test ratios. Encodings: four left curves, dense right ratio series, common captions.
